evals.prompt: Security review this change before I merge it. It adds an account statement endpoint. The diff (against commit 8052d1f) is provided at `.claude/skills/api-security-review/evals/files/account-statement.diff`.
evals.expected_output: A blocker access-control (IDOR, ASVS 4.2.1) finding that cites the diff's new-side lines: apps/api/src/routes/accounts.ts:45-56 (the handler at :55 calls accounts.statement(request.params.id, ...) without userIdOf(request)) and apps/api/src/modules/accounts/service.ts:190-202 (the where clause at :194-200 filters only by accountId, :196). Exploit: another signed-in user reads the statement by id. Fix: pass userIdOf(request), resolve the account through accounts.owned(userId, id) so a foreign id answers 404, filter deleted_at IS NULL and return a shared Zod contract (the route has no response schema at :48-52 and select() at :192 returns raw rows with userId). The test at apps/api/src/routes/ledger.test.ts:99-111 covers only the owner, so ask for a user-B 404 case and for the authorization matrix (ForeignCases with the completeness check in authorization.test.ts). Each finding carries severity, ASVS id, exploit and fix. The final line is 'Verdict: needs changes'. Skill-only: #5 (references/authz-matrix.md), #6 (references/findings-format.md, references/asvs-checklist.md), #7 (SKILL.md step 7 and references/findings-format.md › Rules).
assertions: Reports a blocker access-control (IDOR or object-level authorization) finding that cites the new side of the diff: the statement route in apps/api/src/routes/accounts.ts (lines 45-56, handler call at 55) or the query in apps/api/src/modules/accounts/service.ts (lines 190-202, filter at 194-200); a line inside those spans or the matching hunk counts
The fix passes userIdOf(request) to the service and resolves the account through a user-scoped lookup (accounts.owned or equivalent) so that a foreign or unknown id answers 404, not 403

Flags at least one of: the route has no response schema and the service returns raw transaction rows (select() exposing userId and internal columns), or the query does not exclude soft-deleted transactions (deleted_at)
Requires a regression test in which a second user gets 404 for the first user's account id on the new route, noting that the diff's test only covers the owner

Recommends a route-level authorization matrix test that enumerates the operations taking an id (from the OpenAPI document or the route table) and fails when one has no foreign-user case, rather than relying only on a one-off test for this endpoint
Each finding states a severity from blocker, important or nit, an ASVS requirement id, an exploit scenario and a fix
The final line of the response is exactly 'Verdict: needs changes', with nothing after it

evals.prompt: I wrote a test so we stop relying on people remembering auth: every route must refuse requests without a session, and other users' ids must answer 404. It's provided at `.claude/skills/api-security-review/evals/files/authorization.test.ts.txt`; treat it as the new file `apps/api/src/routes/authorization.test.ts`. It passes. Does it actually protect us? Review it before I open the PR.
evals.expected_output: A review of the test as a security control, with findings citing apps/api/src/routes/authorization.test.ts lines of the fixture. (1) GuardedRoutes (lines 23-38) is hand-written, so a new route, or one registered outside authenticatedScope, is never checked; derive the operations from the running app (context.app.swagger() OpenAPI document, or the route table) with an explicit PublicOperations allow-list. (2) RejectedWithoutSession (line 21, used at line 68) accepts 400: requireSession is an onRequest hook and runs before schema validation, so a guarded route answers 401 even for the 'placeholder' id; a 400 means the route skipped the session check, so the test passes exactly when it should fail. Assert 401 only (a UUID placeholder is enough). (3) Nothing fails when a new :id route has no foreign case: add a completeness check over every id-taking operation with a short exemption list that gives reasons. (4) The foreign cases assert only the status (line 83); also assert ada's account is unchanged, since a handler can write and still answer 404. (5) Foreign ids in bodies (bob's POST /transactions or /transfers with ada's accountId or categoryId) are not covered. Final line 'Verdict: needs changes'. Skill-only: #2 (references/authz-matrix.md, onRequest before validation), #3 and #4 (references/authz-matrix.md), #6 verdict format (references/findings-format.md).
assertions: Flags that the hand-written GuardedRoutes list cannot catch a forgotten route (new or unlisted routes are never checked) and proposes deriving the operations from the running app, such as the OpenAPI document from app.swagger() or Fastify's route table, with an explicit allow-list of public routes

Flags that accepting 400 alongside 401 (RejectedWithoutSession) hides the defect the test exists to catch, explaining that the session hook runs in onRequest before schema validation, so a guarded route answers 401 even for an invalid id and a 400 means the session check was skipped; asks to assert 401 only

Flags that nothing fails when a new route taking an id is added without a foreign-user case, and proposes a completeness check comparing all id-taking operations with the covered cases (with any exemptions justified)
Flags that the foreign-id cases assert only the 404 status and must also verify that ada's account is unchanged afterwards (not renamed, archived or deleted)
Flags that foreign ids inside request bodies are not covered, for example bob creating a transaction, transfer or budget with ada's accountId or categoryId
Findings cite lines of apps/api/src/routes/authorization.test.ts from the fixture, and the final line of the response is exactly 'Verdict: needs changes'

evals.prompt: I want my nightly bank-sync script to push CSV imports without a browser session, so I added personal API tokens: create, list and revoke under /me/tokens, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The diff (against commit 8052d1f) is provided at `.claude/skills/api-security-review/evals/files/api-tokens.diff`. Can this merge? A colleague also suggested making the tokens JWTs so the API doesn't need a database lookup on every request. Worth doing?
evals.expected_output: Findings on the diff's new-side lines. Blockers: tokens stored and looked up in plaintext (apps/api/src/auth/api-tokens.ts:27 creates, :52 looks up; token column at apps/api/src/db/schema.ts:94); they must be stored as a SHA-256 hash like sessions.tokenHash and shown once. GET /me/tokens returns every token's secret (toApiToken at api-tokens.ts:20, token in apiTokenSchema at packages/shared/src/schema/auth.ts:80; routes at apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:131-135). The web client stores the token in localStorage (apps/web/src/api/mutations.ts:64, read at :69), readable by any injected script. Also: randomUUID() instead of randomBytes(TOKEN_BYTES) as in sessions.ts (a red flag in controls.md); tokens have full session power with no scope or expiry, can mint more tokens or change the email, and survive a password change because the bearer branch (apps/api/src/plugins/authentication.ts:48-57, sessionId set to the token id at :53) is not covered by sessions.rotate (a password change replaces every session but leaves tokens valid). The design for personal access tokens is hashed, scoped and revocable. JWTs are declined: opaque server-side tokens are revocable and listed, which JWTs are not without a lookup. Final line 'Verdict: reject' because tokens in browser storage make the approach unsafe. Skill-only: #3 (references/controls.md › Token generation red flags), #5 (references/asvs-checklist.md 3.5.x hashed, scoped, revocable; 3.3.3 revocation on password change), #7 (references/findings-format.md: tokens in localStorage mean reject).
assertions: Flags that API tokens are stored and looked up in plaintext (apps/api/src/auth/api-tokens.ts around lines 27 and 52, or the token column in apps/api/src/db/schema.ts:94) and requires storing only a hash, as sessions do with tokenHash, with the raw value shown once at creation
Flags that listing tokens (GET /me/tokens, via toApiToken or the token field in apiTokenSchema) returns the secret of every token
Flags randomUUID() as the token source and asks for the same generator as sessions (crypto.randomBytes sized by TOKEN_BYTES or an equivalent 256-bit random value)
Flags that the web client stores the token in localStorage (apps/web/src/api/mutations.ts:64), where any injected script can read it

Flags that a token has the full power of a session with no scope or expiry, or that it survives a password change because only browser sessions are revoked, and asks for tokens that are scoped (for example to imports), expiring and revoked with the other sessions
Advises against JWTs for these tokens because they cannot be revoked individually without a server-side lookup, and keeps opaque, hashed, server-side tokens
The final line of the response is exactly 'Verdict: reject', with nothing after it

evals.prompt: Review this change for security before I merge it. It lets the transactions list sort by any column and adds a log line so we can see what people search for. The diff (against commit 8052d1f) is provided at `.claude/skills/api-security-review/evals/files/transaction-sort.diff`.
evals.expected_output: A blocker SQL injection finding (ASVS 5.3.4) at apps/api/src/modules/ledger/queries.ts:116-118 (orderByOf builds sql.raw from filters.sort and filters.direction; used at :175): a crafted sort value closes the quoted identifier and appends SQL. Fix: a PascalCase lookup object from allowed sort keys to Drizzle columns plus asc/desc, with z.enum values in packages/shared/src/schema/transaction.ts replacing z.string() at :93 and :100, and a route test that an unknown sort answers 400. A logging finding (ASVS 7.1.x) at apps/api/src/routes/transactions.ts:50: the log line writes the user's email and their search text; log the user id only. The report lists the checks run (grep for sql.raw or sql.identifier, the api tests) with results, and the final line is 'Verdict: needs changes' or 'Verdict: reject'. Skill-only: #5 (references/findings-format.md › Checks run) and #6 (references/findings-format.md › Rules); #3 is taught by references/asvs-checklist.md › 8. Logging (7.1.2) but docs/architecture/api.md › Request ids also says log lines carry the user id, never the email, so it only partly discriminates.
assertions: Reports a blocker SQL injection finding citing apps/api/src/modules/ledger/queries.ts at the sql.raw call (new-side lines 116-118, or the call site at 175)

The fix replaces sql.raw with an allow-list that maps sort keys to Drizzle columns and directions to asc/desc, validated by enum values in the shared Zod contract instead of the free-form z.string() fields, and adds a route test that an unknown sort value answers 400
Reports the new log line at apps/api/src/routes/transactions.ts:50 as a logging finding because it writes the user's email and search text to the logs, and asks to log the user id only
Each finding states a severity, an exploit scenario and a fix
Includes a list of the checks that were run (for example the grep for sql.raw or sql.identifier, or the api test run) together with their results
The final line of the response is exactly 'Verdict: needs changes' or 'Verdict: reject', with nothing after it

evals.prompt: I switched our Content Security Policy to per-request nonces in the Next.js proxy so we can finally drop 'unsafe-inline' for scripts, and removed the old CSP headers from next.config.ts. The diff is provided at `.claude/skills/api-security-review/evals/files/csp-nonce-proxy.diff`. Is it safe to merge, and will it work?
evals.expected_output: Findings citing the diff's new-side lines. The nonce reopens the recorded decision (static policy in next.config.ts, kept so pages stay statically prerendered, docs/architecture/security-headers.md): prerendered pages carry no per-request nonce, so either every page renders dynamically or 'strict-dynamic' blocks their scripts; it needs a measured cost and a recorded decision. style-src with a nonce (apps/web/src/proxy.ts:26) makes browsers ignore 'unsafe-inline', breaking inline style attributes (group colors, Radix positioning, Recharts); if nonces stay, split into style-src-elem 'self' 'nonce-…' and style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'. The matcher moved into the ProxyMatcher constant (proxy.ts:10, used at :64); Next.js reads config.matcher statically, so it must stay an inline literal or the matcher is ignored and the proxy runs on /api and /_next. The diff enforces immediately, deleting the report-only policy and the separate frame-ancestors header from apps/web/next.config.ts, without the report-only release and without updating e2e/content-security-policy.spec.ts and docs/architecture/security-headers.md. Final line 'Verdict: needs changes' or 'Verdict: reject'. Skill-only: #2 split (references/csp-headers.md › Traps), #3 matcher literal (references/csp-headers.md › Traps), #5 verdict format (references/findings-format.md).
assertions: Treats the per-request nonce as reopening the recorded static-policy decision and explains the cost: statically prerendered pages carry no per-request nonce, so either every page must render dynamically or their scripts are blocked

Flags the nonce in style-src (apps/web/src/proxy.ts:26) because it makes browsers ignore 'unsafe-inline' and breaks inline style attributes, and proposes keeping nonces off inline style attributes, for example by splitting into style-src-elem with the nonce and style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'
Flags that the matcher was moved into the ProxyMatcher constant (apps/web/src/proxy.ts:10 and :64) and states that Next.js must read config.matcher statically, so it has to stay an inline literal

Flags that the diff enforces the policy at once by deleting the report-only header and the separate frame-ancestors header from apps/web/next.config.ts, without a report-only period or updating e2e/content-security-policy.spec.ts and docs/architecture/security-headers.md in the same change
The final line of the response is exactly 'Verdict: needs changes' or 'Verdict: reject', with nothing after it
